# fs

The file system: files, directories, links, permissions.

**World access** — needs a grant (see [embedding.md § The module grant](../../embedding.md#the-module-grant)).

```go
fs := import("fs")
f := fs.create("./out.txt")
f.write_string("hello")
f.close()
string(fs.read_file("./out.txt"))   // => "hello" — read_file answers bytes
fs.stat("./out.txt").size           // => 5
```

The constants are the flags of [`open_file`](#open_file), combined with `|`; the whence of
[`fs.file.seek`](../types/fs_file.md#seek); and the bits of a file mode, the `mode` of [`stat`](#stat).

An open file is an [`fs.file`](../types/fs_file.md): `name`, `read(buffer)`, `write(bytes)`, `write_string(s)`,
`seek(offset, whence)`, `stat`, `sync`, `chmod`, `chown`, `chdir`, `read_dir_names(n)`, `close`.

**Failures.** Everything the world can refuse raises kind `io`, with the operation named in the message:
`(fs.remove) remove /nope: no such file or directory`. A function whose success has no result answers `undefined`.

<a id="chmod"></a>
### `chmod(path, mode) -> undefined`

Set a file's permission bits.

`path` is a `string` and `mode` is an `int`.

<a id="chown"></a>
### `chown(path, uid, gid) -> undefined`

Set a file's owner and group; see [`chmod`](#chmod).

`path` is a `string` and `uid` and `gid` are `int`s.

<a id="create"></a>
### `create(path) -> fs.file`

Create (or truncate) a file.

`path` is a `string`.

<a id="lchown"></a>
### `lchown(path, uid, gid) -> undefined`

Set a symbolic link's own owner and group; see [`chmod`](#chmod).

`path` is a `string` and `uid` and `gid` are `int`s.

<a id="link"></a>
### `link(old_path, new_path) -> undefined`

Create a hard link.

`old_path` and `new_path` are `string`s.

<a id="mkdir"></a>
### `mkdir(path, perm) -> undefined`

Create a directory.

`path` is a `string` and `perm` is an `int`.

<a id="mkdir_all"></a>
### `mkdir_all(path, perm) -> undefined`

Create a directory and every missing parent; see [`mkdir`](#mkdir).

`path` is a `string` and `perm` is an `int`.

<a id="open"></a>
### `open(path) -> fs.file`

Open a file for reading.

`path` is a `string`.

<a id="open_file"></a>
### `open_file(path, flag, perm) -> fs.file`

Open a file with flags and permission bits.

`path` is a `string` and `flag` and `perm` are `int`s.

<a id="read_file"></a>
### `read_file(path) -> bytes`

Read a whole file.

`path` is a `string`.

<a id="read_link"></a>
### `read_link(path) -> string`

Answer the target of a symbolic link; see [`link`](#link).

`path` is a `string`.

<a id="remove"></a>
### `remove(path) -> undefined`

Remove a file or an empty directory.

`path` is a `string`.

<a id="remove_all"></a>
### `remove_all(path) -> undefined`

Remove a file or a whole tree; see [`remove`](#remove).

`path` is a `string`.

<a id="rename"></a>
### `rename(old_path, new_path) -> undefined`

Rename or move a file.

`old_path` and `new_path` are `string`s.

<a id="stat"></a>
### `stat(path) -> record`

Answer a frozen record `{name, mtime, size, mode, directory}` of facts about a file.

`path` is a `string`.

<a id="symlink"></a>
### `symlink(old_path, new_path) -> undefined`

Create a symbolic link; see [`link`](#link).

`old_path` and `new_path` are `string`s.

<a id="temp_dir"></a>
### `temp_dir() -> string`

Answer the system temporary directory.

<a id="truncate"></a>
### `truncate(path, size) -> undefined`

Truncate a file to `size` bytes.

`path` is a `string` and `size` is an `int`.

<a id="o_append"></a>

<a id="o_create"></a>

<a id="o_excl"></a>
### `o_excl -> int`

<a id="o_sync"></a>

<a id="seek_cur"></a>
### `seek_cur -> int`

The [`fs.file.seek`](../types/fs_file.md#seek) whence that counts the offset from the current position.
